newsitem.title: USA: US power pool files new system operator plan.
newsitem.headline: US power pool files new system operator plan.

text.p: The Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) power pool filed a revised proposal to the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to set up an Independent System Operator for the Mid-Atlantic power market.

Nine utility members of PJM, grouped as the Supporting Companies, last December filed a power pool plan under the commission's regulations, requiring utilities to open their transmission lines to all competing power producers.
PECO Energy Co, backed by power marketers, filed a competing plan, which outlined a different scheme for setting charges to customers during periods of high energy demand.
The FERC in February urged the rival groups to work out a compromise.

Under their revised plan, to satisfy the commission, the Supporting Companies proposed to set up an unaffiliated governing board to oversee the independent system operator to ensure that no one player or group could control transmission operations and planning.

The group said it clarified its plan to use locational marginal pricing -- fees based on transmission paths at specific points -- rather than rolling congestion charges into a single pool-wide fee as proposed by PECO.
The group also modified its plan to maintain reliable power supplies in the event local power markets are opened to competition and customers start buying power from new suppliers.
The PJM group said its independent system operator would run an hourly spot market to set market clearing prices for power supplies.
